tools: page fetch (WebFetch) for the NIGC Gaming Tribe Report PDFs
log.limits: gaming-entity: no facts. None of the official bulk lists reached gives tribal gaming commission or enterprise names in a usable form (the NIGC Gaming Tribe Report text has contact blocks, but the fetch tool only returned summaries; facility names are kept in the gaming-operation notes instead). gaming-operation: only partial coverage (167 nations). The current NIGC map keeps facility data behind a logged-in REST endpoint, which I did not access. The NIGC Gaming Tribe Report PDFs (2025-06-17 alphabetical; 2024-12-10 by state) now return 404 to curl, and the Wayback Machine is blocked here; the page-fetch tool returned only the first part of each report (alphabetical A through Leech Lake; by state Alabama through Minnesota and a few others), and names were machine-extracted, so nations later in the alphabet or in later states are missing even if they game. A missing gaming-operation fact does not mean the nation has no gaming. gaming-compact: the Office of Indian Gaming list covers 28 states and 1,196 actions; its Tribe column is misaligned with the compact title in about 50 rows (for example Lumbee shown for Mashantucket Pequot secretarial procedures, Nansemond for Narragansett, Navajo for Burns Paiute), so facts use the nation named in the title and say so in the note (confidence medium). Two status values fall outside the contract enum: 'disapproved' (31 rows) and 'secretarial-procedures' (26 rows), kept so the lead can decide; 'Extensions' rows are recorded as 'approved' with a note. Mashantucket Pequot (Connecticut) operates under secretarial procedures, not a compact. Status 'in-effect' and 'expired' were never assigned because the list does not say whether a compact is still in force. The listed date is the date the Office of Indian Gaming gives (often the Federal Register publication or effective date), stored as 'approved'. Minnesota Chippewa Tribe bands (Bois Forte, Fond du Lac, Grand Portage, Leech Lake, Mille Lacs, White Earth) hold their own compacts and ordinances; the roster has only minnesota-chippewa-tribe, so their facts are attached there with the band named in the note (confidence medium). Dispute resolution: one representative compact per state was read (two in Michigan and South Dakota); several are old (1990-1995) and later amendments may have changed the clause; Wisconsin's 1992 text was revised for some nations by later amendments; Minnesota's summary covers the video games of chance compact only (blackjack compacts not summarized); California's summary reflects the recent compact form, while many California nations still hold 1999-era compacts with a different dispute section. Nations with only 'state model compact; nation-specific text not checked' facts should be verified against their own compact. Not covered: Alabama, Texas and Alaska nations have no compacts in the list (Poarch Band, Alabama-Coushatta, Kickapoo Traditional Tribe of Texas and Alaska nations game under class II or other arrangements); no compact list entries were found for some nations known to game (for example Mohegan's later documents, Oneida Indian Nation), beyond what the list shows.
log.narrative: Compacts: scraped all 48 pages of the Office of Indian Gaming compacts list with curl (bia.gov did not block curl this time), parsed state, tribe column, title, document link, Federal Register link, status and date for 1,196 rows, then turned the 665 linked Federal Register documents into volume-page citations through the Federal Register API. Rows without a link were matched to a citation only when exactly one 'Indian Gaming' notice was published on the listed date. Names were matched to roster ids by normalized exact match, a reviewed list of spelling variants, and a scored fuzzy match with manual review of every non-exact match; where the list's Tribe column and the compact title disagreed the title was used. Ordinances: parsed the NIGC gaming ordinances table (321 rows) and recorded the original ordinance date and every amendment date with their document links. Operations: the NIGC Gaming Tribe Report PDFs were only reachable through the page-fetch tool, which returned partial machine-extracted text, so gaming-operation facts are medium confidence and partial. Dispute resolution: downloaded one current or representative compact per state from the Office of Indian Gaming list, extracted the text with pdftotext, read the dispute-resolution section and wrote a one-sentence neutral summary with the section locator. The summary is attached to the representative nation's own compact fact (cited to that compact document), and repeated for each other nation with an approved or deemed-approved compact in that state, noted 'state model compact; nation-specific text not checked', confidence medium.
